cards.title: The Silent Alarm
cards.setup: Every night Tom sets three alarms on his phone. One morning none of them ring, he wakes up two hours late, and he is delighted.
cards.solution: Tom works in a bakery and the alarms are for his early shift. The night before, his daughter had secretly swapped shifts with his colleague so he could sleep in on his birthday, and she turned the alarms off. He woke up late to breakfast already on the table.

keyFacts.text: The alarms were for an early work shift.
His daughter turned the alarms off on purpose.

hints: Tom was not in trouble for being late.
Think about what day it was.

cards.title: The Wet Letter
cards.setup: Maria receives a letter, reads it, and immediately puts it under a running tap. Afterwards she smiles and pins it to the fridge.
cards.solution: Her nephew had written the letter with a "magic" pen whose ink only shows up when wet, as part of a game they play. Under the tap the hidden message appeared: a drawing and the words "Coming to visit on Sunday!".

keyFacts.text: The letter was written in ink that only appears when wet.
The letter came from a child in her family.
The message was good news about a visit.

hints: Maria wasn't trying to destroy the letter.
The letter looked blank at first.

cards.title: Two Tickets, One Seat
cards.setup: A woman buys two cinema tickets for herself, sits in one seat for the whole film, and leaves the other seat empty. She says it was the best money she spent all year.
cards.solution: She had broken her leg skiing and it was in a cast that would not bend. In a normal cinema row she could not sit at all, so she bought the seat next to hers as well and rested her leg across it for the whole film.

keyFacts.text: She had a broken leg in a cast.
She needed to keep the leg stretched out.
The second ticket was for the seat next to her.

hints: The empty seat was not empty for nothing.
Think about something she couldn't bend.

cards.title: The Overdue Book
cards.setup: A library book is returned forty years late. Instead of charging a fine, the librarian frames the book and hangs it on the wall.
cards.solution: The book was returned by a now-famous author, who had borrowed it as a child and credited it with making them want to write. They returned it with a handwritten note on the inside cover, which made it a treasure for the small town library.

keyFacts.text: The borrower had become a famous author.
The book inspired them as a child.
They added a handwritten note inside the book.

hints: Who returned it mattered more than when.
Something was added to the book before it came back.
